title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: iGOT MISSION KARMAYOGI IN WEST BENGAL
body_text:
Presently 90,276 civil servants from West Bengal have been onboarded on the iGOT Karmayogi platform. The Government of West Bengal has not yet signed the tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) under Mission Karmayogi.
So far, eight draft Capacity Building Plans (CBPs) have been prepared for Government of West Bengal's priority departments. The iGOT Karmayogi digital learning platform hosts over 5,600 courses covering domain, functional and behavioural competencies. These courses are available for consumption for all registered users including those from West Bengal. As on date, 10,493 course completions have been recorded by learners from West Bengal. Further, all employees of the Central Government and officers of the All India Services, including those serving in West Bengal have to mandatorily complete prescribed courses annually on iGOT which gets reflected in their respective APARs for the corresponding period.
The DoPT, along with the other implementing agencies of Mission Karmayogi – Capacity Building Commission (CBC), and SPV Karmayogi Bharat (KB) are supporting the Government of West Bengal in its capacity building initiatives including handholding for the adoption of the role-based competency framework, onboarding on the iGOT platform, and integrating iGOT with other HR platforms/tools. A Programme Coordinator from CBC and an Assistant Manager from KB serve as Nodal Officers for the state of West Bengal for this purpose. DoPT also supports targeted capacity building activities in all states/UTs, including West Bengal, through the Training for All (TFA) scheme.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

NKR/AV

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

enrichment.summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that 90,276 civil servants from West Bengal have been onboarded onto the iGOT Karmayogi digital learning platform, though the West Bengal government has not yet signed the tripartite MoU under Mission Karmayogi. Eight draft Capacity Building Plans have been prepared for the state's priority departments, and 10,493 course completions have been recorded by West Bengal learners out of over 5,600 courses available on the platform. DoPT, the Capacity Building Commission, and Karmayogi Bharat are extending handholding support to the state, including nodal officers for coordination.
enrichment.context:
Mission Karmayogi (National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building, NPCSCB), launched in 2020, aims to prepare Indian civil servants for future roles by enhancing their efficiency through role-based, competency-driven training. Its digital backbone, iGOT Karmayogi, hosts courses across domain, functional and behavioural competencies, and is mandatory for Central Government employees and All India Services officers, whose course completion is linked to their Annual Performance Appraisal Reports (APARs). The scheme envisages a tripartite MoU among the Centre, states, and Karmayogi Bharat (the SPV managing the platform) to enable states to adopt the framework, though implementation varies across states based on political and administrative alignment with the Centre's initiatives.

This reply highlights the federal and voluntary nature of civil service capacity building reforms in India, where states like West Bengal have significant civil servant participation on the platform despite not formally signing on to the mission's institutional framework. It reflects the broader theme of Centre-state cooperation in governance reforms, capacity building as a tool for administrative efficiency, and the increasing digitization of public sector training through platforms like iGOT, which is relevant to India's civil service reform trajectory since the 2nd Administrative Reforms Commission recommendations.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Mission Karmayogi:
1. It mandates all state governments to sign a tripartite MoU before their employees can access the iGOT platform.
2. Course completions by Central Government employees and All India Services officers on iGOT are reflected in their APARs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release clarifies that West Bengal has not signed the MoU yet its civil servants can still access and complete courses on iGOT, showing signing an MoU is not a precondition for platform access. However, it explicitly states that mandatory course completion by Central Government employees and AIS officers is reflected in their APARs, making statement 2 correct.

prelims_questions.question: The 'iGOT Karmayogi' platform is associated with which of the following?
options: National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (Mission Karmayogi)
prelims_questions.explanation: iGOT Karmayogi is the digital learning platform under Mission Karmayogi (National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building), launched to build competency-based training for civil servants.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the objectives of Mission Karmayogi in reforming India's civil services training ecosystem. What challenges arise in ensuring uniform adoption of this initiative across states?

Examine the role of digital platforms like iGOT Karmayogi in enhancing capacity building of civil servants in India. How can such initiatives be strengthened to ensure better outcomes at the state level?
